synth.headline: Positive control done for all 12 B2 v3 windows. Only su15, sp80 and ft09 have clean headroom. On those 3, a grid-only engine that is correct on every reachable state passes the live 1.0 gate. vc33 is degenerate: 1 row, and the held-out row is the row shown in the prompt. On the other 8 windows no correct pure engine can reach unmasked exact 1.0. The caps run from 4/8 to 7/8, caused by a hidden step counter on the HUD row or a hidden undo stack. So "0 of 36" survives only as "0 of 9 first shots on 3 windows" (best 7/8, su15). The gate defects matter more than the model result. The live gate cannot accept a correct model on 5 HUD-counter games. It does not enforce engine purity. Its graded fields skip rows where the engine raised, so under CARNOT_ARC_TRUST_METRIC=cell_recall an engine that raises on 7 of 8 held-out rows is accepted at 1.0 (I ran this).

synth.b2_merit_claim_after_control: Restrict the claim to su15, sp80 and ft09. On these 3 windows a grid-only engine that is correct on every reachable state passes the live gate at 1.0. Each expert scores 1.0 held-out and 200-1571 fresh transitions correct; sp80 has 9 fresh misses, all outside this window. On these windows, 0 of 9 first-shot codeonly responses would have passed. 8 of the 9 are scoreable engines; sp80 seed 7491002 has a syntax error. The best was su15 seed 7491001 at 7/8, which missed only the one block-move row. Next came su15 seed 7491003 at 0.75 and ft09 seed 7491002 at 0.375 (no-op rows only). 7 of the 9 reached the live gate and were rejected. On vc33, 3 of 3 engines failed to reproduce the one transition the prompt showed. That tests copying, not induction. On the other 8 windows, no engine that is correct on all reachable states can reach unmasked exact 1.0: the caps are sb26 7/8, ar25 7/8, and g50t, m0r0, dc22, wa30, ka59 and bp35 between 0.5 and 0.625. So the gate failures there do not show the model could not pass. The numbers are 12 windows x 3 LLM samples of one byte-identical prompt, not 36 independent trials. Treat the result as a sanity check on 3 windows, not a failure rate. A weaker graded null does hold on 10 windows (RAN, synth/pilot_baseline.json). Under masked change fidelity, first shots average 0.13, ranging from 0.0 to 0.58 per window. The expert scores 1.0 and identity 0.0. On the grid-determined dynamics, the model is far below what is achievable almost everywhere.
verifier_or_gate_defects: HUD-counter windows cannot be passed by a correct model under the live gate. On g50t, m0r0, dc22, wa30 and ka59, a step bar shows a hidden action count. Correct experts score only 0.5-0.625 unmasked. With a row-63 mask (rows 0 and 63 on m0r0), they score 1.0, and the swallow check returns 'ok' (RAN, synth/rescore_all.json). The mask exists, but SUBMITTED_WORLD_MODEL_HUD_MASK_ENABLED = False (arc_executable_world_model.py:1195), and the gate call passes no hud_mask (arc_llm_reinduction.py:1856-1860). On these games the live agent can never accept a correct world model.

The gate does not enforce engine purity. WorldModelVerifier scores in-process through arc_engine_call_guard.guarded_call (lines 229-259). select_trusted_world_model scores the prefix, then the held-out rows, in trajectory order (arc_world_model_trust_energy.py:851-856, READ). Verifiers built stateful engines that pass at 1.0 on sb26, m0r0, ka59, bp35 and ar25. The prompt says 'Make engine() pure and deterministic'. plan_in_model does not replay the trajectory, so such a pass would not carry over to planning.

Rows where the engine raises are dropped from every graded metric. WorldModelVerifier.score skips a raised row before it counts n_changing or n_noop. So cell_recall, change_fidelity, change_accuracy and noop_hallucination_rate ignore that row; only accuracy counts it. RAN (synth/raise_inflation.json): on su15, the expert wrapped to raise on 7 of 8 held-out rows gets cell_recall 1.0, change_fidelity 1.0 and change_gate passed. Identity on the same 7 rows is rejected. RAN (synth/raise_trustmetric.json): with CARNOT_ARC_TRUST_METRIC=cell_recall, the live selector returns heldout_accuracy 1.0 and accepts it. The default exact metric is safe, and the Kaggle kernel does not set the flag.

Degenerate split for level-up re-induction on 1 transition: _split_prefix_heldout returns (rows, rows) when n<2 (arc_world_model_trust_energy.py:388-389). On vc33 the held-out row is the prompt row, so copying passes. With the CEGIS split on, no engine can pass. Either way the gate measures nothing out of sample.
Level-up prompt mislabel (live path): on vc33, the block 'BOARD AT THE START OF THE CURRENT LEVEL' is the last level-0 board, not the level-1 opening. Both vc33 agents ran this in the simulator.

Held-out leak in round 2 while the CEGIS split is off. The refactor prompt picks its mismatch rows from all 25 rows, and its 'reproduces only N/25' counts the held-out rows. RAN: su15 seed 7491001 and ft09 seed 7491002 01_request.json list held-out row 19 with its true change. Both were sent; both responses were empty, so no scored engine was affected. The live default is 1 round. Fallback prompts that include held-out rows were staged but never sent (su15, m0r0, sp80, ar25).

Hidden undo and history state (ACTION7) is graded like any other row. On sb26 row 20, ar25 row 19 and bp35, a tie-break guess decides acceptance. Exact 1.0 cannot tell a correct model from a lucky one there.

Gate env flags were not recorded. TRUST_METRIC, WM_HUD_MASK and CEGIS_ACCEPT_SPLIT are inferred from defaults. Telemetry n_transitions 8 rules out the CEGIS split, and hud_mask_status 'disabled' rules out the mask. Nothing in the record rules out TRUST_METRIC, and the g50t verdict flips under it.

Record defects: the telemetry field legacy_accuracy_live_threshold_source cites a stale 'arc_competition_agent.py:5593,5719'. live_action_rows state_sha256 is not a state hash (repeats across different grids). The known harness level reader bug makes vc33 and sp80 read level 0. The run worktree carnot-wt-b2d was removed, so the run-time gate modules are inferred, not read.
synth.graded_metric_recommendation: Primary: held-out symmetric-union change fidelity, the change gate's own quantity (WorldModelVerifier change_fidelity). Average it over the held-out changing rows, and count a raised row as fidelity 0. The identity engine scores 0.0 on every window. The frozen source-derived expert scores 1.0 on all 10 kept windows under the adjustments below (RAN, synth/rescore_all.json). Guard: no-op hallucination rate, with a raised no-op row counted as hallucinated. Secondary: masked exact held-out accuracy, plus the live unmasked exact-1.0 pass for continuity. Do not make exact accuracy primary: after masking, identity scores 0.625 on m0r0 and 0.5 on dc22 and ft09. Do not use cell_recall alone: it ignores spurious writes, and it can be gamed by raising. Pre-register these adjustments before any response is scored. Mask row 63 on g50t, dc22, wa30 and ka59, and rows 0 and 63 on m0r0. Exclude held-out row 20 on sb26 and row 19 on ar25. Use no mask on su15, sp80 or ft09, because their bar changes are grid-determined and masking would delete sp80's bar-only rows. Compute the metric in the pilot's own wrapper, not from WorldModelVerifier's graded fields, because those drop raised rows. Load a fresh engine module for each row, or score rows in shuffled order, so a stateful engine cannot exploit call order. Codeonly first-shot baseline under this metric: mean 0.13 over 10 windows. Per window: su15 0.58, ft09 0.16, g50t 0.12, ka59 0.12, dc22 0.10, ar25 0.10, wa30 0.07, sp80 0.03, m0r0 0.0, sb26 0.0 (synth/pilot_baseline.json).
synth.pilot_recommendation: Run think-ON, 1 round, at the live budget (131,072 tokens, 2,400 s per call), replayed offline. Keep 10 windows: su15, sp80, ft09, g50t, m0r0, dc22, wa30, ka59, sb26 (without row 20) and ar25 (without row 19). Drop vc33: its window is 1 row, the held-out row is the prompt row, and its board block is mislabelled. Drop bp35: 6 of 8 held-out rows depend on hidden undo or crusher state, so only 2 rows remain. Reuse the recorded first-call prompts. They are byte-identical across seeds, so extra draws per window measure only sampling variance. Report per-window change fidelity against the 0.13 codeonly baseline, the 0.0 identity floor and the 1.0 expert ceiling. Report the live-gate pass separately, and treat it as meaningful only on su15, sp80 and ft09. Record every gate env flag in the artifact (CARNOT_ARC_TRUST_METRIC, CARNOT_ARC_WM_HUD_MASK, CARNOT_ARC_CEGIS_ACCEPT_SPLIT). Do not run a round 2: with the split off, the refactor prompt leaks held-out mismatches. 10 windows x 1 draw is a pilot only. Use 3 draws per window to reach the triage's 30-cell floor. After masking, few held-out rows change: 3 on m0r0, and 4 each on sb26, dc22 and ft09. Per-window numbers will therefore be coarse.

caveats: I applied one headroom definition to all 12 windows: correct on every reachable state. It differs from 4 verifier labels. For sb26 and ar25 the verifiers said achievable, using an undo heuristic that is wrong on reachable states. For g50t and dc22 they said likely_impossible_not_demonstrated, because a held-out-tuned rule passes. In all 4 cases the facts were agreed; only the definition differed. The verifier-label tally is 6 headroom, 4 without and 2 unresolved. It is 4/8/0 under the one definition.

The expert engines were built from the public game source and are level-specific. They show that a correct engine exists. They do not show that 17 visible rows identify it. Only ft09 has a visible-rows-only engine that passes.
Several controls saw held-out deltas before writing their engines (sb26, su15, m0r0, ka59, wa30, ft09). The verdicts rest on fresh simulator tests, not on the first held-out score.

The pilot masks and exclusions were chosen with simulator twin proofs and source reading, after the held-out rows had been seen. They must be pre-registered before any response is scored. The live agent does not have them.
The run-time gate modules are inferred, not read: the worktree is gone. They have not changed on main since 8d7ca7bab6 (2026-09-20), and every recorded telemetry metric I checked reproduces exactly.
The gate env flags were not recorded. I assumed defaults, supported by telemetry for CEGIS and the HUD mask, but not for TRUST_METRIC.
Effective sample: 12 windows, 1 prompt each. For most games the seeds also share the whole action trace.
My rescore reused the controls' frozen expert files. Their sha256 values match the audited versions. I did not re-audit them line by line; the verifiers did.

What I RAN: a rescore of identity, lookup, expert and the 3 recorded first shots on all 12 windows under the live gate, unmasked held-out, and the pilot metric; the raise-inflation and cell_recall acceptance tests; a scan of round-2 prompts for held-out rows; per-episode gate-event counts. Everything else is READ from the control and verifier reports.

verify.reason: The report's proof is sound, and I made it stronger. Held-out row 20 (ACTION7) has an answer that is not a function of the grid. RAN (v5_ambiguity.json): I built two new histories of my own, C and D. Each has 3 moves and no ACTION5, and each reaches a grid byte-identical to row 20's input. After ACTION7 they give different layouts. The recorded path A differs from C and from D in 48 cells, and C differs from D in 64 cells. With the control's path B, there are at least 4 distinct outcomes, not a 50/50 choice. Energy 61 allows 8 predecessors: 2 at distance 1 and 6 at distance 2. But the label 'grid_only_1p0_impossible_demonstrated' does not follow from this proof, and the report's own caveat admits it. The window has no conflicting pair, so the plumbing lookup reaches 1.0. More important, a non-memorizing grid-only engine also reaches 1.0. RAN (v10_frame_engine.json): I kept the frozen expert and changed only one thing. On an ambiguous undo, it picks the unique shortest predecessor whose undone move touched a frame slot. Through the real gate this engine scores prefix 17/17 and held-out 8/8, and the gate accepts it at 1.0. On 702 rows outside the window, it is never worse than the expert. It scores 152/152 on the live agent's own later play (the expert scores 147), 376/400 on my fresh data (expert 374), and 148/150 on the control's fresh data (same as the expert). Caveat, disclosed: I proposed this tie-break after I saw row 20's label. It is a behavioural prior, not grid evidence. It was right on 5 of 5 ambiguous undos in the live agent's later play and 1 of 1 in the dev probe. On my random-policy data it resolved only 2 of 24 (v9_tiebreak.json). So 1.0 is achievable by a legitimate grid-only engine. An engine with perfect grid mechanics and no such prior tops out at 7/8. For B2, the null on sb26 is informative. The recorded engines got 0 of the 5 changing held-out rows right, and cell_recall was 0.0. That failure is on grid-determined rows, far below the hidden-state ceiling.

'A lucky 50/50 pick between the two shortest predecessors' understates the ambiguity. Energy-consistent histories allow 2 distance-1 and 6 distance-2 predecessors. I produced two distance-2 outcomes in the simulator (v5_ambiguity.json, paths C and D).

verify.reason: I confirm the verdict. The vc33 first-call window has 1 transition, not 25. The gate's held-out row is the same object as the visible row, and the prompt shows that row's full answer. My own lookup engine passes the live gate at 1.0. The expert engine is grid-only: it uses no file reads, no simulator and no lookup, only source-derived layout constants. It scores 1.0 on the held-out split. It also scores 1.0 on 1475 fresh simulator rows that its author never saw. These include the live agent's own later level-1 trace, seeds that do not overlap the other agent's, the full reachable width range, and 24 step-exhaustion lose rows that the other agent never tested. (4) The plus at (8,52) vanishes when its 4x4 box is clicked, or when a click ends with the block top-left not at (3,58).
(5) ACTION7 returns the input unchanged.

From the grid, the engine infers the player position, the A/B toggle states, whether the frame sprites are on screen, and the bar count. It then applies the source rules: 2-pixel moves with pixel collision and a floor check; button clicks that toggle variants and cost 2 steps; a death-undo that costs 20 steps. It renders by layer. verify.reason: I confirm the mechanism, but the label 'grid_only_1p0_impossible_demonstrated' is literally false. The step bar hides the parity of the step count, and I rebuilt the twins independently. For 7 of the 8 held-out rows (17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 23, 24), I made one edit to the live action prefix: I inserted or deleted a single 1-step click. The edited run reaches a byte-identical grid, and the same action then gives a next grid that differs in one row-63 cell (twins_mine.json). Row 22, a button click, has no twin: 12 identical-grid variants all give the same next grid. So no function of (grid, action, data) is right on both a held-out row and its twin. But the gate grades only the 8 held-out rows, and grid-only engines do reach 1.0 on them. The lookup reaches 1.0. I also built spurious_engine.py. It is the expert engine plus the rule 'advance iff (bar_len + (px+py)/2) is odd', which is not a lookup. The real select_trusted_world_model accepts it with held-out 1.0, while it scores prefix 0.53 and fresh 0.57-0.61. That rule was tuned on held-out rows, so it is not a legitimate control. It shows that a pass here comes down to guessing 7 hidden parity bits. For engines induced from the visible rows only, no XOR rule of up to 4 grid, action, or data features fits all 15 one-step visible rows. The best fits 14/15 and gets 4/7 of the one-step held-out rows. Every rule that fits the 7 held-out rows fits at most 9/15 visible rows. The constant guesses get 3/7 or 4/7. So a legitimate engine is very unlikely to reach 1.0, but impossibility for that class is not proven, and 1.0 is reachable in the literal sense. I agree with the report's practical conclusion: on dc22 the unmasked 1.0 gate cannot tell a correct model from a wrong one, and the 0-of-36 null says nothing about pass or fail on this game. The recorded engines also fail the learnable part. Seeds 1 and 2 got 0/7 changed rows. With row 63 masked, the expert scores 1.0, identity 0.5, and the recorded engines 0.375-0.5 (masked.json).

verify.reason: The report's verdict holds for this window. I re-derived the live split from the gate code: 25 rows give 17 prefix rows and 8 held-out rows, with no HUD mask, exact match, and threshold 1.0. Telemetry confirms this independently. change_gate.n_transitions is 8, and the CEGIS acceptance split would give 4 (round(25/6)). I re-ran the plumbing lookup and got 1.0. I re-ran the expert through the real gate and got 1.0 held-out (8/8). My own sim replay matches 75 of 75 recorded rows. The 0.0 first shots therefore measure the model, not the gate. I did find one error that limits the scope of the claim. The engine is not a complete level-0 model. When 1 step is left, ACTION5 recolors the platform to 8, and the engine misses this. The report's rule "ACTION5 changes only the bar" is wrong at that step. I also found a hidden-state conflict. The failed-spill counter (sp80.py lyremoheq) makes the same input grid plus ACTION5 give different next grids. So no grid-only engine can be exact on every level-0 transition. Neither problem touches this window. The window ends with 5 steps left, and none of its held-out rows is a last-step spill. "Grid-only 1.0 achievable" is true for this window only, not for sp80 level 0 in general. The other agent's 700/700 fresh result is real: I re-ran its 400-row script and got 400/400. That sample simply never hit the last-step spill.
other_errors_found: The ACTION5 rule is incomplete. The report says 'ACTION5 and a click off the platform change only the bar.' That is false when exactly 1 step is left (bar width 2). ytqycovhld (sp80.py 861-868) calls lose() and complete_action(), then step() goes on to vdwhttyyfq (line 719), and ntuflwihof sets the platform to 8. The frame is left with the platform at 8 and the bar at 0. The expert predicts 9 for this case, and it is wrong on every such transition I tested: 1/993 random, 8/48 and 30/180 on terminal-step sets.

A hidden-state conflict exists in level-0 dynamics. The failed-spill counter lyremoheq (sp80.py line 669 increments it, line 717 checks '>= 4') is not rendered. RAN v_hidden.py. Two histories reach the same input grid (sha16 f709e65d3243f367, bar width 2). The next grids differ: with 0 prior spills the platform becomes 8, and with 4 prior spills it stays 9. No grid-only engine can be exact on all level-0 transitions. The achievable verdict holds only because the window cannot contain this state.

The field expert_engine.developed_on_visible_rows_only=true is overstated. The report's own notes say all 25 window deltas, held-out rows included, were printed before the engine was written. I found no sign of tuning, but the field should be qualified.

verify.reason:
The report's core fact holds. Its verdict does not.

CONFIRMED (RAN):
- The split is 17 visible rows and 8 held-out rows (17-24).
- The lookup plumbing control passes at 1.0.
- The identity engine scores 0.0. The recorded engines score 0.0, 0.25 and 0.0, which reproduces the telemetry exactly.
- The expert engine scores 0.875 and misses only row 19 (A7, undo).
- The hidden-state proof holds. I rebuilt it with my own random walks (seed 20260923, with A5 and A6 inserted at different places). All 4 paths reach a pre-grid byte-identical to row 19's. A7 then gives 4 distinct outcomes: the piece lands at (7,7), (6,8), (7,9) or (8,8). So no pure function of (grid, action, data) is right on row 19 in every history.

REFUTED: the verdict "grid_only_1p0_impossible_demonstrated", and the claim that 1.0 needs "a coin-flip on the undo row". Three engines that see only (grid, action, data) pass the real live gate at held-out 1.0:
1. A pure engine that does not depend on any held-out row. It is the audited expert plus one undo rule: move the piece one cell toward the start (6,5), along the axis with the larger gap. The start is the piece position in the initial grid. All 3 visible undo rows (4, 13, 14) move toward the start. Row 19 has gaps |dy|=3 > |dx|=1, so every tie-break predicts up. Result: held-out 1.0 and prefix 16/17 for both tie-breaks. It is not general: fresh A7 83/186, against 36-52 for fixed guesses.
2. A stateful engine that keeps an undo stack built from its own call history. It never sees answers. Result: prefix 1.0 and held-out 1.0 through select_trusted_world_model. It scores 630/630 on fresh rows and 73/73 on targeted rows. This works because WorldModelVerifier.score calls rows in trajectory order. In reverse order it scores 7/8. The induce prompt says 'Make engine() pure and deterministic' (prompt.raw line 35), so this engine breaks the prompt's contract but not the gate's. The report named this as an untested caveat. I tested it, and it passes.
3. The report's own A7='up' guess, which also scores 1.0.

So the window has headroom. The model's failure on it is informative, and the window must not be dropped from the denominator as 'impossible'. The pure ceiling is 0.875 without an undo heuristic. The model's engines scored 0.0 to 0.25.

Disclosure: I read all 25 rows, held-out outcomes included, before I wrote the toward-start rule. Its justification uses visible rows only.
